newsitem.title: USA: R.R. Donnelley to meet with Rainbow-PUSH.
newsitem.headline: R.R. Donnelley to meet with Rainbow-PUSH.

text.p: R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co said it will meet with Rev. Jesse Jackson's Rainbow PUSH Action Network on Monday, December 9 to address complaints of racism and age discrimination.

"The company values its reputation as a good employer that treats all employees fairly and equally, regardless of their position in the company," R.R. Donnelley said in a statement. The company said it does not tolerate discrimination of any type.
R.R. Donnelley, a commercial printing company, is the target of a $500 million federal class action suit that alleges race discrimination based on layoffs, promotions and wages.
The company had said the lawsuit was filed in connection with a 1993 plant closing and it denies the allegations, labelling them as "reckless, false and inflammatory."

This operation was closed as a result of Sears, Roebuck & Co's decision to discontinue its twice-yearly "big-book" catalogs, which represented the primary work performed at the facility, the company said.
